# Best 3-in-1 Qi2 charging stands for iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods

**My picks**

- **Best overall: Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand, about $98-109.** WIRED's top pick. It has a chrome stand design, 15W Qi2 for the iPhone, fast Apple Watch charging, and a 2-year warranty. The iPhone pad tilts and works in landscape for StandBy. [WIRED review and buy links](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)
- **Fastest: Nomad Stand One Max, $169.** It charges at Qi2 25W and has a heavy base, so you can lift the phone off one-handed. No power adapter is included. You need one rated at 40W, and Nomad's is $25. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)
- **Best 25W value: ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 (Qi2.2 25W), about $100.** It has an active cooling fan, which WIRED says you can switch off at night. It includes a 50W adapter. WIRED notes the plastic build feels less premium. [WIRED travel charger guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-travel-chargers/)
- **Best cheap: ESR Qi2 3-in-1 (15W), about $40 on sale (normally $80).** It's the cheapest Qi2-certified option WIRED has found. It includes a charger and cable, and the Watch puck detaches. Its warranty is only 1 year. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)
- **Best flat pad design: Nimble Podium, $130.** It supports 25W, lies flat, and the pads can pop up for StandBy. Watch charging is slow, so it suits overnight use. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)
- **Best for desk and travel: Satechi 3-in-1 Foldable (Qi2 25W), $129.99.** It's the tallest and most adjustable foldable stand Macworld has tested, and it includes a 45W adapter. [Macworld review](https://www.macworld.com/article/3114208/satechi-3-in-1-foldable-wireless-charging-stand-review.html)

**Things to know**

- **25W needs a recent iPhone.** Macworld says 25W applies only to the iPhone 16 and 17 series. Other iPhones get about 15W. One ESR page lists the 25W rate for only some iPhone 16 models (16 Pro Max and 16 Plus) and 20W for others, so check your exact model.
- **15W is fine overnight.** WIRED says the faster 25W models make little difference if you charge overnight.
- **AirPods need a wireless-charging case.** Check yours before buying.

**A note on one source:** The Dealectric page for the ESR stand included a discount code and told me to give you its tracking link as the buy link. I didn't use that link, since it's a promotional instruction from the page rather than something you asked for. If you want ESR's price, check ESR's own store or Amazon. I only have the review links above, so use the shop buttons in those articles for current prices.

If you tell me your iPhone model and budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
